entities.summary:
Aymer de Lusignan was a significant figure in the history of the Plantagenet dynasty, serving as Lord of Cyprus and playing a crucial role in the establishment of the Kingdom of Cyprus in the 13th century. A grandson of King John, Aymer de Lusignan was instrumental in the recapture of Cyprus from the Sultan of Egypt in 1268, securing his family's claim to the island and cementing their dominance in the Mediterranean region. His leadership and strategic alliances with European powers, including the Kingdom of England and the Holy Roman Empire, helped shape the course of medieval politics and diplomacy.

Aymer de Lusignan's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, with his descendants continuing to play a prominent role in the politics and culture of the region. His influence can be seen in the development of the Kingdom of Cyprus as a major power in the Mediterranean, and his family's connections to European royalty and nobility.

The impact of Aymer de Lusignan's actions can be seen in the subsequent history of the region, including the rise of the Ottoman Empire and the eventual fall of the Kingdom of Cyprus to Turkish rule in the 20th century.

Aymer de Lusignan's story is one of intrigue, politics, and power, offering a fascinating glimpse into the complex web of alliances and rivalries that shaped medieval Europe and the Middle East.
